ai.title: Log data truncates error message query and params to keep cause
ai.summary: The shared Axiom log-row pipeline in `common/src/util/log-data.ts` now caps `error.message` to `MAX_ERROR_MESSAGE_CHARS`, caps `error.query` to `MAX_ERROR_QUERY_CHARS`, and replaces oversized `error.params` arrays with a [n params omitted] count string inside `errorToJson`, while still preserving `error.name`, the leading `cause`, and a sliced `stack`. This addresses the 2026-10-02 ad-revenue rollup failure where a 522 KB `DrizzleQueryError` was cut at `MAX_LOG_DATA_BYTES` and the Postgres `cause` never reached Axiom. Two new tests cover the huge-query truncation and the short-query param retention.

eli5.text: When a database error is so large that recording every detail would be wasteful and slow down logging, the system now keeps the most important parts and drops the bulky ones. Engineers who investigate problems still get the error type, a trimmed stack trace, and the root cause from Postgres, but the giant SQL statement and its long list of input values are replaced with short summaries. ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.11 to 0.2.12 release bump
ai.summary: The `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was updated from `0.2.11` to `0.2.12`, marking the release-bump commit 0cb91045. The release members span functional changes in the CLI, SDK, and common packages, including timezone handling, BigQuery message row lookup columns, agent-publisher trust gates, and streak day accounting tied to the account timezone reset.
ai.evidence: The diff for `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` shows the `version` field changed from `0.2.11` to `0.2.12` in a release-bump commit (0cb91045). The commit contains no source changes, only the manifest version bump, and the release members list includes functional updates across CLI, SDK, common, and agent-runtime packages.

eli5.text: This release is a packaging bump (0.2.11 to 0.2.12) that updates the Freebuff CLI installer; the version label itself changed, and the release notes carry only a version bump with two prior README model-catalog additions and a Freebucks timezone handling change as the user-facing notes. The final catalog state confirms the picker now includes /todo along with the regular model list, and the limited-access catalog was widened so Space Bunny Alpha shows up for limited users; the model list adds Space Bunny Alpha and retires DeepSeek V4 Pro from the deep-reasoning slot in favor of GLM 5.3 Flash. The Freebucks timezone change means the CLI no longer trusts a wrong or remote clock: it skips reporting a timezone when the machine is SSH/dev-container based or when the OS reports a fixed-offset zone instead of the user's real location, so daily Freebucks resets follow your actual day instead of your host's. Other changes are infrastructure-only: BigQuery tracing adds lookup columns and a stable dedupe key, ad-serving telemetry gains a precomputed-score experiment and geo-tier fields, error logging now truncates oversized SQL statements and params so Postgres failures actually reach logs, the SDK refuses to run remote agents whose code or MCP servers come from untrusted publishers, the Windows Git-Bash finder now also locates Git installed by GitHub Desktop, and local dev config got new ignored credential files for billboard asset storage. Everyday impact is limited to users of Space Bunny Alpha in limited mode, people who were getting the wrong Freebucks reset time while working over SSH or in a remote container, and anyone relying on Freebuff Desktop's billboard ad slots, plus contributors whose local test setup now isolates real API keys; the rest is backend reliability and ad-serving instrumentation. To summarize plainly: the headline is a version-number bump, and the only things users actually notice are Space Bunny Alpha becoming available in limited mode and Freebucks resets now following your real timezone instead of your host's.

testNames: a crashed writer no longer prevents deleting a saved connection
recovery preserves a live owner even when its lock is old
competing processes recover a legacy PID lock without losing writes
throwing from an operation releases its lock for the next writer

facts: Publish an already-complete PID atomically. Creating an empty lock and then writing its owner leaves an unrecoverable lock if killed between.
EPERM (including another user's process) is not evidence of death.
Recover PID locks without allowing two reapers to unlink a successor's lock.

A second filesystem lock would itself survive a crash. A loopback listener is a short-lived, kernel-released reaper mutex on every supported OS. Key it by the observed PID, so aliases of the configuration path share the mutex. Collisions only defer recovery; they never allow concurrent reapers.
Re-read under the mutex: another reaper may already have removed the old lock and a writer may now own the pathname. Never expire a live PID by age.
entries.title: SDK update: byok
entries.summary: New files: `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts`.

ai.title: SDK recovers stale BYOK connection lock via PID check
ai.summary: `createBunByokMetadataStore`'s `withLock` now publishes the owning PID to an atomic lock candidate and uses `fs.link` to claim `connections.lock`, so a process killed between creating the lock file and writing its PID no longer leaves an unrecoverable lock. `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` adds `recoverByokLock`, which calls `recoverByokLock(lock)` on `EEXIST`: it reads the lock's owner, treats `EPERM` (including another user's process) as not dead, uses a loopback listener on port `49152 + (Number(owner) % 16384)` as a short-lived kernel-released reaper mutex keyed by the observed PID, and re-reads the owner under that mutex before unlinking the lock so it never expires a live PID by age or removes a successor's lock. Tests cover a crashed writer not blocking connection deletion, recovery preserving a live owner even when its lock is old, competing reapers not losing writes, and an operation that throws releasing its lock.
ai.evidence: New file `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` exports `recoverByokLock`; `sdk/src/byok.ts` imports it and calls `await recoverByokLock(lock)` from within the `withLock` method of `createBunByokMetadataStore` when `fs.link(candidate, lock)` throws `EEXIST`. The `withLock` implementation now writes `String(process.pid)` to a per-call `connections-lock-<uuid>.tmp` candidate with { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 } and hard-links that candidate to `connections.lock` via `fs.link(candidate, lock)`, replacing the prior `fs.open(lock, 'nx')` + `handle.writeFile` approach.
ai.unknowns: Whether the new lock scheme changes the on-disk lock path shape or how the Desktop settings UI surfaces the updated retry message.
